known_red_gates.tooling: go-licenses v2.0.1 built with go1.27.1 - exactly the version the Makefile pins. make install-tools considered the binary current and did not rebuild it, so this is not local toolchain drift.

known_red_gates.disposition: Recorded, not fixed. R02 preserves observed state and does not block archival on unrelated cleanup. This is a licence-scanning tooling failure, not a licence violation: no forbidden, restricted, or unknown licence was reported, because the scan aborted before classification.

post_snapshot_updates.subject: signing_preflight.forge_verification
post_snapshot_updates.change: The GPG key is now registered on the Codeberg account and its ownership is verified (key_id 7796A98BEA4F4647, verified=true, signing subkey 23583C11192A9DF4 can_sign=true). The address bot@keystone-core.io was added to the account but is NOT yet activated: Codeberg returns HTTP 500 on the verification step. Until it activates, Forgejo binds no email to the key, so signed commits render as unverified.
post_snapshot_updates.remaining_blocker: Activation of bot@keystone-core.io on the Codeberg account (Codeberg-side 500).
post_snapshot_updates.expected_on_resolution: Forgejo computes signature verification from current key state at render time, so already-pushed signed commits are expected to display as verified retroactively without re-signing. Spot-check the R02 freeze commit to confirm.
post_snapshot_updates.gates: Blocks nothing before R05. R05's archive tag needs forge-visible verification.
post_snapshot_updates.chosen_route: Add bot@keystone-core.io to the account (route B) rather than adding a uid to the key, keeping one committer identity continuous with Generation 1 history.

post_snapshot_updates.subject: signing_preflight.forge_verification
post_snapshot_updates.change: Resolved. Codeberg's HTTP 500 on email verification proved persistent, so route B was abandoned for route A: a second uid 'Keystone-core Bot <keystone-bot@keystone-core.io>' was added to the key and made primary, keeping the original bot@keystone-core.io uid. The key was deleted and re-added on Codeberg (now id 154525) because Forgejo reads a key's uid emails once at add time and offers no refresh. It now reports the bound email keystone-bot@keystone-core.io as verified. The git committer email was changed to match. The signing subkey expiry was extended from 2027-06-01 to 2029-09-08 in the same export.
post_snapshot_updates.residual: None observed. Codeberg reports all three signed R02 commits (388b25990, 98d7a2f1e, 0f1967f68) as verified with reason 'keystone-bot / 23583C11192A9DF4', including the two committed under the still-unactivated bot@keystone-core.io. Forgejo matched the signature to the key's owner rather than requiring the committer address to be a bound email. Verified against a control: unsigned commits on the same repository correctly report verified=false, reason gpg.error.not_signed_commit.
post_snapshot_updates.future: bot@keystone-core.io was deliberately left as a uid on the key. It costs nothing and keeps the older committer identity associated with the key if Codeberg's verification endpoint is ever fixed.
post_snapshot_updates.r05_impact: Cleared. The archive tag must be created with tagger email keystone-bot@keystone-core.io.
post_snapshot_updates.verification_method: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/commits/{sha}?verification=true - the verification object is omitted unless that query parameter is passed, so its absence is not evidence of an unsigned or unverified commit.

tag.delete_probe: deliberately not performed: an unblocked delete would destroy the signed tag object, and recreating it would produce a different object id with a different signature and timestamp

protection.probe_design_note: Two earlier probe designs produced no evidence and are recorded so a later auditor does not repeat them. Force-pushing the SAME sha reports 'Everything up-to-date' and never contacts the server. And --dry-run pushes report success even against a protected ref, because Forgejo enforces protection in the pre-receive hook, which a dry run does not reach. Only a real update or delete attempt against a different value is conclusive.

unique_history.finding: 2172 commit objects are reachable only from local refs/replace/ mappings and from no ref on the forge. Their CONTENT, however, is not unique.
unique_history.cause: A git filter-repo run on 2026-02-20, evidenced by .git/filter-repo/{commit-map,ref-map,already_ran,suboptimal-issues}. It removed four commits whose only files were development scratch notes (CHECKPOINT.md, TUI_MONITOR_TEST_RESULTS.md, SESSION-SUMMARY.md) and the resulting hash change cascaded to every descendant.
unique_history.evidence: Across 120 sampled original/replacement pairs the trees are identical, and across 150 pairs the author name, author email, committer name, committer email and subject are identical. Only parentage differs. commit-map records 2173 rewritten, 16 unchanged and 4 removed.
unique_history.correction: An earlier revision of this record implied the bundle held ~2000 commits of otherwise-lost history. That overstated it. The commit objects are unique; the work they contain is preserved in the current history under different SHAs. What is genuinely unique to the pre-rewrite history is the four scratch-note commits and the old-to-new SHA mapping, both of which the bundle holds.
unique_history.not_a_secrets_rewrite: gitleaks scans the full reachable history (2886 of 2904 non-merge commits; a replace-only commit was spot-checked directly) and reports no leaks. The rewrite removed working notes, not sensitive material.
unique_history.decision: Not pushed to the forge. Maintainer decision, on the grounds that republishing ~2000 content-duplicate commits works against R08's minimal baseline while preserving nothing the current history and this bundle do not already hold.

before.note: All twelve required contexts come from .forgejo/workflows/ci-fast.yml. Nothing from ci-full.yml was ever required.

after_intended.rationale: A required context whose workflow R08 deletes can never be reported, and main would become permanently unmergeable. The new context is produced by a workflow that needs no Go toolchain, so it keeps working once the module is gone.

risk_window.description: Between this switch and R08, the Generation 1 Go code still exists but is gated only by the minimal baseline. ci-fast.yml keeps running, so failures remain visible; they simply stop blocking a merge.
risk_window.accepted_by: maintainer, on the plan's own terms: R06's acceptance requires that legacy contexts no longer block
